goal: Evolve repo-docs-intelligence-bootstrap with the reusable document authority, ADR, implementation-plan, evidence, review, wiki-decision, validation, and optional derived retrieval patterns proven in DuckCrab, without copying DuckCrab domain vocabulary, forcing every artifact into small repositories, or creating a second canonical store.

userStories.title: Establish the portable Repo Docs link contract
userStories.description: As a repository maintainer, I want Repo Docs memory to use portable Markdown links while preserving legacy wikilink input and bounded evidence traversal.
acceptanceCriteria: Repo Docs uses descriptive relative Markdown links by default while llm-wiki-bootstrap remains Obsidian-wikilink-first.
Existing wikilinks remain compatible input and no mass conversion is required.
AGENTS guidance limits relevant traversal to two additional hops and twelve pages and verifies canonical targets.
The validator rejects missing and outside-repository local Markdown links without false failures for URLs, anchors, code examples, footnotes, references, nested lists, or balanced paths.
Full pytest, focused validator tests, Ruff, skill validation, and independent review pass.

userStories.title: Add an adaptive documentation authority lifecycle
userStories.description: As a repository maintainer, I want one lightweight Repo Docs profile that promotes only sufficiently important work into ADRs, plans, evidence, reviews, and wiki decisions.
acceptanceCriteria: The skill defines a reusable authority chain spanning live code and tests, current canonical docs, accepted ADRs, intelligence contracts, plans/evidence/reviews, derived wiki memory, and optional search indexes.
Promotion rules distinguish small changes, reusable analyses, durable structural decisions, multi-stage implementation, verification claims, and reviews without pre-creating every optional directory.
Minimal templates exist for ADR, implementation plan, evidence, review, and wiki decision, with decision status separate from implementation status and wiki decisions explicitly non-canonical.
New repositories may default to docs/adr while existing flat or custom ADR locations remain supported without migration or key renaming.
No DuckCrab-specific BUILD/ASK/CHECK, Pack, MCP, or ontology vocabulary is introduced; full tests, Ruff, skill validation, and template contract tests pass.

userStories.title: Validate activated decision and evidence chains
userStories.description: As a repository maintainer, I want the validator to catch broken lifecycle claims only when those optional document surfaces are actually activated.
acceptanceCriteria: The validator accepts small repositories with no ADR, plan, evidence, review, decision, repo-map, intelligence, or retrieval directories.

Activated ADRs have unique decision identities, valid decision and implementation statuses, resolvable supersession/plan/evidence references, and implemented claims backed by implementation and verification evidence.
Activated wiki decisions remain source_of_truth=false and resolve their canonical ADR or canonical decision source plus relevant evidence when implementation is claimed.
Docs portals expose activated decision/evidence/review indexes and stale completed or superseded plans cannot masquerade as the current next action.
Focused minimal, mature, transitional, and drift fixtures plus full pytest, dependency-light execution, Ruff, skill validation, and independent review pass.

userStories.title: Add optional derived Repo Docs retrieval
userStories.description: As a maintainer of a documentation-heavy repository, I want an opt-in SQLite FTS and Markdown-link index that reduces context reads without becoming truth or a mandatory bootstrap dependency.
acceptanceCriteria: A bundled dependency-light CLI can rebuild, status-check, search, traverse bounded links, and doctor a derived SQLite index from AGENTS.md, docs Markdown, and wiki Markdown only.

The index stores heading chunks, descriptive Markdown-link edges, content fingerprints, and FTS5 data; it is disposable, atomically rebuilt, and never indexes source-code bodies or becomes canonical truth.
Repo Docs guidance keeps retrieval opt-in and non-blocking, recommends it only for measured scale or repeated long-document reads, and leaves CodeGraph/LSP/rg responsible for code navigation.
SQLite-off repositories and missing optional retrieval state remain fully valid; no ONNX, RRF, ANN, JSONL ontology, workflow engine, or runtime database integration is added.
Focused rebuild/search/link/stale/off tests, full pytest, dependency-light unittest, Ruff, skill validation, generated-profile smoke, and independent review pass.

userStories.title: Certify mature and minimal repository compatibility
userStories.description: As a skill maintainer, I want final dogfood evidence that the evolved profile fits DuckCrab-like mature repositories without burdening minimal or legacy repositories.
acceptanceCriteria: Read-only DuckCrab dogfood inventories and validates its canonical docs, flat ADRs, plans, evidence, reviews, repo-map, and wiki decisions without requiring relocation or domain-specific vocabulary.
Minimal and transitional fixtures prove optional-surface absence, existing manifest keys, flat ADR paths, and legacy wikilinks remain supported.
Skill guidance, templates, validator, eval expectations, tests, and optional retrieval documentation agree on one unified adaptive profile.
The final impact report distinguishes absorbed reusable patterns, deliberately excluded DuckCrab-specific behavior, checked-but-unchanged surfaces, remaining cautions, and exact validation results.

Full pytest, dependency-light tests, Ruff, skill validation, fixture validation, DuckCrab read-only dogfood, git diff checks, and final independent code review report no Critical or Important findings.
